title: What If a Country Switched Road Sides Overnight? Sweden Did in 1967

scenes.text: What if every car in a country swapped sides of the road at the same minute? Sweden did.
In 1955, 83 percent of Swedes voted to keep driving on the left. Parliament switched anyway: every neighbour drove on the right, and 90 percent of Swedish cars had left-hand wheels.
Sunday, September 3, 1967, 4:50 am: all traffic stopped. Drivers crept across and waited ten minutes. At 5:00, they drove on.
350,000 road signs were swapped, 8,000 buses got doors on both sides, and every household got a 32-page booklet.
That day: 157 minor accidents, none fatal. The Monday after had fewer crashes than usual. Everyone was driving scared.
Within six weeks, accidents were back to normal. People adapt faster than you'd think, and get careless just as fast.

description:
What if an entire country switched from driving on the left to driving on the right in a single morning? Sweden did it on 3 September 1967, Dagen H.
In a 1955 referendum 83 percent had voted against it, but neighbouring countries drove on the right and over 90 percent of Swedish cars were left-hand drive. At 4:50 am all traffic stopped, moved over and restarted at 5:00. Around 350,000 signs were changed and about 8,000 buses refitted. 157 minor accidents were reported that day, none fatal; the Monday after had fewer accidents than usual, but within about six weeks insurance claims were back to normal.
What should we run through next?
